raise_justifications.INV-AUTH-1-agent-env-hardening: +55 to restore the fork's agent subprocess environment hardening, which the 2026-08-01 sync dropped for the second time (PR #98, PR #100): a 9-key allowlist for the Node child environment and Firebase token delivery through a 0600 file instead of OMI_AUTH_TOKEN. It sits in this file because the control is the spawn path itself, and PiMonoWiringTests pins the forbidden and required patterns to this source. Splitting the helpers out would move the tripwire off the spawn site and give one control two owners.
raise_justifications.INV-AUTH-1-agent-token-file-cleanup: +4 to clear the auth token file on the unexpected-termination path. This is the same control as INV-AUTH-1-agent-env-hardening: the Firebase token reaches Node through a 0600 file, and stopProcess and cleanupFailedStart already removed it, but handleTermination did not, so a crashed or OOM-killed child left a readable token on disk. The cleanup belongs beside the other teardown this coordinator owns, because a separate observer of child death would give one secret's lifetime two owners. Raised by hand to exactly +4 rather than via --update-baseline, which would have granted both target files 10% headroom.
raise_justifications.INV-CHAT-1: Chat-first rich-block handling, answer submission, and task completion stay in the existing provider while its shared lifecycle extraction remains bounded.
raise_justifications.INV-CHAT-1-runtime-payload: +8 for the bundled-runtime start refusal. A build shipped without Contents/Resources/pi-mono-extension accepted every chat turn and died four seconds later with "pi-mono process exited (code 1)"; the refusal has to sit beside the other start-refusal preconditions this file already owns, because a second observer would give one failure two owners. The reason and its wording were moved out to AgentRuntimePayload.StartRefusal, which is why this is +8 rather than +13 — the coordinator keeps only the decision to stop, not the explanation.
